title: Probe, Reobserve, Abstain: Interventional Feasibility Certificates for Unseen Object Pairs
hook: For target-reference pairs with identical initial visible PointMaps but different hidden clearances, a passive geometry adapter cannot identify which requested relation is executable, whereas a bounded probe-response transcript can. The headline metric is unsafe-execution rate at matched execution coverage, which should decrease when the gate uses interventional evidence rather than static geometry alone.
hook_shape_rationale: Shape (a), surprising empirical reveal, is admitted because unsafe-execution rate at matched coverage is predicted to separate passive and interventional arms on PointMap-matched fixtures. Shape (c) was viable because the gate leaves frozen OpenPI pi0.5 weights untouched, but it was rejected because parameter minimalism is not the load-bearing claim.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf establishes behavior on geometrically incompatible target-reference pairs for which the requested relation cannot be executed, rather than always returning a pose, trajectory, affordance chain, or action chunk; this is a class property whenever relation feasibility depends on contact geometry, with rigid registration and insertion as primary instances 鈥?stakes: forced execution can damage hardware or waste real-robot trials, and excluding infeasible pairs makes success metrics and learned generalization claims systematically optimistic.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by relocating the feasibility signal from passive pair geometry to a dynamically reacquired probe-response locus, then using the controlled-diagnostic companion to score PointMap-matched pairs with a full-state oracle independent of the gate; corpus support is thin in robot manipulation, and C01's closest exemplars are security and detection systems.

core_mechanism: Interventional Feasibility Gating (IFG) is restricted to rigid-object relations with a preregistered bounded library of guarded probe primitives and defines feasibility relative to that library and the frozen OpenPI pi0.5 executor. At probe step k, an Intel RealSense D455 observation is segmented by SAM2 into fresh target and reference masks and converted into current PointMaps P_T^k and P_R^k; IFG never carries a surface index or world-frame contact coordinate from step k-1 into step k. From only P_T^k, P_R^k, the relation r, and the current gripper pose, it constructs the safe set U_k of Cartesian micro-twists whose visible swept-volume clearance exceeds c_safe = 10 mm, selected by a 5-15 mm commissioning sweep, and whose guarded force is capped by F_max = 5 N, reduced whenever the robot site's certified limit is lower. Two small response-density models p_F and p_I, trained on independently labeled feasible and infeasible probe episodes, predict the distribution of a response under the feasible and infeasible hypotheses conditioned on r and probe type but not on a raw PointMap embedding. IFG chooses u_k in U_k by the largest predicted Jensen-Shannon disagreement between p_F and p_I, executes it, stops on the force guard, and immediately reacquires P_T^(k+1) and P_R^(k+1) before any next action. Its response y_k is the commanded gripper-frame twist together with measured gripper displacement, target and reference centroid displacement from the two fresh SAM2 masks, joint-torque impulse, post-probe visible clearance, and a mask-reacquisition flag; these are transcript values, not future spatial anchors. The central object is O_K = {(r, type(u_k), y_k)} for k up to B_probe and its evidence I_K = sum_k log[(p_I(y_k|r,type(u_k)) + epsilon_den)/(p_F(y_k|r,type(u_k)) + epsilon_den)], with epsilon_den = 1e-4 selected by held-out likelihood-stability sweep and B_probe = 3 selected from 1-5 on the held-out cost-risk curve. Thresholds tau_I and tau_F are chosen on a held-out oracle-labeled calibration set to minimize deferrals subject to alpha_risk = 0.10, a user-set maximum empirical selective-risk bound: I_K >= tau_I yields infeasible and blocks pi0.5, I_K <= tau_F yields feasible and releases pi0.5, and all other cases defer. The companion diagnostic constructs RoboCasa/MuJoCo and modest real Franka Panda fixture pairs with matched initial visible PointMaps but different occluded inner clearances, labels simulation episodes using full-state exhaustive rollouts over the same bounded primitive library and real fixtures from preregistered manufactured clearances, and compares IFG with a parameter-matched passive PointMap adapter, a minimum-clearance rule, and a same-transcript MLP. Because only realized intervention responses enter I_K and every action coordinate is discarded before reobservation, IFG is neither a re-encoding of the passive geometry-to-label map nor a stale global-anchor program.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 - PREMISES ledger:
P1: Single-view PointMaps can be observationally identical while occluded inner clearance changes relation feasibility; RoboCasa/MuJoCo hidden-geometry variants and paired manufactured fixtures make this premise directly checkable.
P2: Guarded micro-probe responses carry feasibility information beyond the initial PointMaps; untested — falsification target, and the load-bearing evidence variable I_K measures that separation.
P3: SAM2 can preserve target/reference instance identity over the bounded probe motions often enough to reacquire fresh PointMaps; failures are observable through the reacquisition flag and cause defer rather than reuse of a stale anchor.
Observation-model premise: probes are selected adaptively by a fixed U_k/disagreement policy, so samples within an episode are not IID; calibration and test use the same frozen probe policy, and any exchangeability claim is only across held-out pair episodes, not across probe steps.
ESTIMAND: selective risk is the probability, over held-out unseen target-reference pair episodes under the fixed probe policy, that the frozen pi0.5 execution fails the relation or violates a collision/force rule conditional on IFG releasing execution; coverage is the probability that IFG releases rather than defers.
BLOCK 2 - NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT: the runnable naive version trains a parameter-matched MLP or LoRA adapter from the initial dense target/reference PointMaps and relation directly to a feasibility logit, then executes pi0.5 when that logit passes a calibrated threshold. Branch (i): it silently assumes the pre-action visual geometry is sufficient, which is false by construction on matched-visible-PointMap fixtures whose occluded clearance differs; IFG confronts the missing information by intervening and measuring the response rather than encoding the same static inputs differently. Active sensing and sequential testing are standard tools, but this instance couples query choice to a strict force/clearance budget and to object motion that invalidates spatial references, so the domain-specific contribution is the discard-reobserve-reconstruct protocol plus risk-calibrated abstention under a shrinking safe probe set; if a same-transcript classifier matches IFG, the result is honestly application-grade.
BLOCK 3 - Design rationale: the removal test supports one deep gap, so the oracle construction, active probe, and abstention rule are one feasibility module rather than separate sibling mechanisms. A variable phase graph, a static dense adapter, and a hand-coded geometric clearance test were rejected respectively because they repeat an occupied scaffold family, cannot resolve the controlled observational alias, and cannot use measured contact response; the design also avoids regression to key-frame correspondence, PDDLStream-style task-and-motion planning, and fixed object-relative trajectories.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Build the modest ProbePair-Oracle resource in RoboCasa/MuJoCo by rendering target-reference variants with matched initial visible PointMaps and different occluded clearances, label each episode with full-state exhaustive rollout over the preregistered guarded primitive library, and manufacture a small Franka Panda fixture set whose hidden clearances determine the real labels independently of IFG.
2. Install the frozen OpenPI pi0.5 checkpoint as the downstream executor and the frozen SAM2 checkpoint plus Intel RealSense D455 depth stream as the observation path; IFG reads masks, point clouds, joint torques, and gripper state but no pi0.5 logits or gradients.
3. For every calibration episode, construct U_k from the current masks and depth, execute one guarded probe, discard its sampled surface coordinates, reacquire both masks and PointMaps, and store only (r, probe type, measured response y_k, oracle label).
4. Fit p_F and p_I on the calibration transcripts, freeze them, and select epsilon_den, B_probe, tau_F, and tau_I by their stated held-out rules; never tune thresholds on the evaluation fixtures.
5. At deployment, reacquire P_T^k and P_R^k from the current observation, build U_k anew, and output defer immediately if SAM2 loses either role or U_k is empty rather than falling back to an old coordinate.
6. Select the probe with maximum predicted response-model disagreement, execute it under c_safe and F_max, and record y_k from the before/after observations and robot sensors.
7. Recompute the PointMaps and safe set after every object motion, append the coordinate-free response to O_K, update I_K, and repeat only while neither threshold is crossed and the B_probe budget remains.
8. If IFG returns feasible, release the unchanged current observation and relation to frozen pi0.5 for normal action-chunk execution; if infeasible, issue a no-execute decision with O_K as the evidence record; if deferred, request a new view or human decision without moving toward the task contact.
9. Evaluate the complete pathway against the passive PointMap adapter, minimum-clearance rule, and same-transcript MLP at matched execution coverage, and run response-permutation and full-state-oracle controls to attribute downstream safety to pair-bound intervention evidence.
falsification_prediction: On RoboCasa/MuJoCo and the preregistered Franka Panda fixture pairs, compare IFG with a parameter-matched passive dense PointMap feasibility adapter, a minimum-clearance rule, and a same-transcript MLP, then run frozen pi0.5 only on episodes each gate releases. If the candidate works, unsafe-execution rate and relation-failure rate decrease at matched execution coverage while defer rate remains reported rather than hidden. The one load-bearing variable is I_K, the accumulated pair-bound interventional response evidence; the negative control permutes y_k records across target-reference pairs while preserving each pair's initial PointMaps and commanded probe types. Under that control, the downstream unsafe-execution rate should rise toward the best passive baseline, whereas replacing y_k with the simulator full-state response oracle is a positive-control upper bound; no numeric outcome bar is asserted.
compute_budget: 8 A100-80GB GPU-days for RoboCasa/MuJoCo trace generation, response-density fitting, and frozen-pi0.5 evaluation; 24 Franka Panda robot-hours plus fabrication of the modest ProbePair-Oracle fixtures; $0 paid API.

EasyInsert predicts a relative pose and runs a fixed coarse-to-fine insertion process, whereas IFG tests feasibility before releasing any executor and reports selective risk on matched-visible-geometry negative pairs; this delta is an abstract-only inference because its fetched method section is empty.

what_step_was_missed: EasyInsert would have needed to replace unconditional relative-pose execution with an independently calibrated pre-execution probe-response test whose coordinates are discarded and recomputed after every object motion, including labeled incompatible pairs and an explicit abstention outcome; this is an abstract-only inference because the fetched method section is empty.
